Brian L Bengs

Independent candidate for United States Senator, South Dakota · Challenger

Retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and attorney; former National Park Service ranger at Wind Cave National Park

Brian Bengs is a Hot Springs resident, a Navy veteran and retired Air Force JAG officer who later taught at Northern State University and worked as a park ranger at Wind Cave National Park. He was the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in 2022 and lost to John Thune with about 26% of the vote. In April 2025 he announced a 2026 run as an independent, and in April 2026 the Secretary of State certified him for the November ballot with 4,311 valid petition signatures.

Where Bengs stands

Artificial intelligence
Supports halting new AI data center construction until the federal government sets guardrails. Says he will oppose any legislation that does not give local communities a workable way to say no to data centers, and pledges not to accept AI data center money.
National security
Opposes the U.S. war with Iran. Says he would not have voted to enter it, would not vote to continue it, and that its objectives were never clearly defined because Congress did not do its job.
Border security and immigration
Proposes an immigration overhaul that pairs border security with more legal immigration, which he calls crucial to economic growth. Supports birthright citizenship and opposes ending it by executive order.
Gun rights
Describes himself as a gun owner who supports the right to bear arms for self-defense and favors what he calls reasonable gun safety measures.
Abortion
Says he respects a woman's right to choose and supports abortion restrictions after viability, with exceptions for the life or health of the mother.
Taxes
Proposes to 'unrig the tax code' so the wealthiest pay what he calls their fair share. Also supports balancing the federal budget and paying down the national debt.
Campaign finance
Supports a constitutional amendment to overturn Citizens United and limit unlimited corporate and super PAC political spending.
Term limits
Supports a constitutional amendment limiting senators to two terms and House members to six terms. Pledges to serve no more than two terms himself.
Party caucus
Has pledged not to caucus with either party if elected.
